common_name: Vision in White Astilbe (White-Plumed Vision Series Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in consistently moist, organically rich soil in partial shade; Vision in White (US Plant Patent PP18,965) was introduced in 2007 by Dutch breeder Johannes van Veen, bred from a cross of 'Vision' and 'Dusseldorf', and is the white-flowered member of the compact Vision series.

directions: Plant crowns so the top of the rhizome sits 1-2 inches below the soil surface in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Vision in White produces thick, fluffy, linen-white plumes in mid to late summer held above a mound of glossy, dark bronze-green, finely cut foliage, giving strong color contrast typical of the compact Vision series bred by Johannes van Veen. It reaches its full mature size within two to three growing seasons and is generally deer and rabbit resistant, though browsing can occur during periods of food scarcity. Astilbe does not tolerate drought and will brown and decline quickly without steady moisture, so mulch well and water regularly through the growing season, especially in a hot, humid Gulf South summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom.

common_name: Dark Side of the Moon Astilbe (Dark-Leaved Purple-Flowered Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in consistently moist, organically rich soil in partial shade to shade; Dark Side of the Moon (US Plant Patent PP35,461) is an Astilbe chinensis-type hybrid introduced by Proven Winners in 2023 and named the 2026 Proven Winners Perennial of the Year, notable as the only dark-leaved astilbe paired with purple flowers on the market.

directions: Plant crowns so the top of the rhizome sits 1-2 inches below the soil surface in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full shade; Dark Side of the Moon forms a mound of rich mahogany-purple to nearly black foliage that emerges yellow with a dark margin before deepening with a glossy sheen, topped by dark stems carrying raspberry buds that open into rosy violet-pink flowers in summer. Unlike most astilbe, it tolerates somewhat drier and sunnier sites in northern climates where moisture stays consistent, but in the Gulf South it performs best with reliable shade and steady moisture to avoid scorch. Astilbe does not tolerate drought, so mulch well and water regularly through the growing season. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or plant divisions in spring; Volkerfrieden (meaning 'peace of nations') is a German-bred Belladonna Group delphinium, a hybrid strain between Delphinium grandiflorum and D. elatum noted for its branching, floriferous habit and reliable rebloom.

directions: Plant in rich, moist, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun to light partial shade, staking as needed to protect the branching flower spikes from wind. Volkerfrieden bears single to semi-double flowers in a deep gentian blue leaning toward purple, carried on a highly branched inflorescence typical of the Belladonna Group, where side spikes are nearly as prominent as the main raceme, giving a looser, airier, more floriferous look than the dense spires of Pacific Giant or Elatum strains. It blooms from June into early autumn and readily produces a second flush of flower stems if cut back after the first bloom. All parts are toxic if ingested. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Dusky Maidens Delphinium (Mulberry-Mauve New Zealand Hybrid)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or sow in fall for cool climates; Dusky Maidens is a New Zealand-bred Elatum-type delphinium strain grown for its unusual smoky mulberry, mauve, and dusky-rose color range rather than the typical blues and purples of the genus.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun, staking tall flower spikes to protect them from wind and summer storms. Dusky Maidens produces strong, densely flowered spires of stout, double and semi-double blooms in unusual smoky mulberry, mauve, and dusky-rose tones, a striking departure from the typical blue-violet palette of Pacific Giant and Elatum delphiniums, developed as part of the New Zealand strain of delphinium breeding. In warm climates it is typically grown as a cool-season annual or short-lived biennial since it declines quickly in summer heat and humidity, while in cooler zones it persists as a short-lived perennial with excellent drainage. All parts are toxic if ingested. Cut spent flower spikes back hard after the first bloom flush to encourage a possible secondary round of shorter spikes later in the season.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or sow in fall for cool climates; Sungleam is a Blackmore & Langdon-bred Elatum delphinium strain and Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit recipient valued for its unusual soft lemon-cream flower color.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun, staking tall flower spikes to protect them from wind and summer storms. Sungleam bears towering spires of large, semi-double, soft buttery lemon-cream flowers with a yellow 'bee,' an unusual warm-toned counterpart to the typical blues and violets of the genus, bred by the renowned English delphinium house Blackmore & Langdon and holding the Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit. In warm climates it is typically grown as a cool-season annual or short-lived biennial since it declines quickly in summer heat and humidity. All parts are toxic if ingested. Cut spent flower spikes back hard after the first bloom flush to encourage a possible secondary, shorter round of flowering later in the season.
